correctness.rationale: For every 2<=m<=n-1 and 0<alpha<1, the Gaussian pencil almost surely has a one-dimensional kernel representation. Direct coordinate elimination derives all generalized Ritz values and the unique nonpersistent eigenvector. An independent unitary Gaussian rotation yields the normalized complex-Cauchy density and p<2 moment formula, with divergence at p>=2. Independent gamma variables yield a Beta(1,m-1) refined quotient; elementary beta integration and harmonic expansion establish its mean and logarithmic behavior, and Beta-to-exponential convergence plus an exact median prove the iff high-dimensional consistency threshold. All denominators are almost surely nonzero. Direct numerical and integral checkers in VERIFY.py reproduce finite consequences without asserting experimental proof of limits.

value.rationale: The motivating modern square-sketch eigenvalue method has high-probability quadratic refined accuracy but suffers sharp heavy-tail constants. This theorem supplies exact risk calibration: finite but log-inflated mean refined error compared with the deterministic Ritz value, an infinite second moment for the unrefined complex Ritz eigenvalue, and a necessary-and-sufficient combined sketch-size/trial-angle condition for consistent refinement. These are motivated algorithmic stability properties and exact interpretable asymptotics beyond generic distribution substitutions.
